title_en: Commentary on al-Mughnī al-Mufīd — Tape Nine
body_ar: وهذه البدع هي بنيات الطريق يمينا وشمالا، وهي الأبواب المفتحة التي عليها الستور، وكل من دخل بابا منها صعب خروجه منه بعد ذلك، وفي كل باب منها شيطان يدعو إليه ويزينه للناس فإذا تمسك به الناس وأخذ به عدد منهم أصبح سنة لديهم وأصبح منكره منكرا للسنة، فحينئذ يظنون المنكر معروفا والمعروف منكرا ويتمسكون بذلك المنكر، مع كون الشرائع والفطر تردها،
body_en: These innovations in religion (bidʿah) are the side-paths branching off right and left; they are the opened doors with curtains hung over them. Whoever enters one of those doors finds it hard to come out of it afterwards, and at every one of those doors there is a devil calling to it and making it seem fair to people. Once people hold fast to it and a number of them take it up, it becomes a 'sunnah' in their eyes, and whoever rejects it becomes, in their eyes, one who rejects the sunnah. At that point they take what is wrong (munkar) to be right and what is right (maʿrūf) to be wrong, and they cling to that wrong — even though the revealed laws and sound human nature reject it,

flags.context: The title of the series, appearing in the title of articles 502–516.
options: al-Mughnī al-Mufīd (left untranslated as a work title)
The Sheikh's commentary series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd
flags.note: Article 516 shows the series expounds Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, and article 508 quotes the base text in verse, so al-Mughnī al-Mufīd appears to be a versification (naẓm) of that book rather than a separate work by the Sheikh. The Sheikh's office should confirm the work and its author before the title is translated or expanded anywhere in the corpus; it has been left untranslated for now.

flags.arabic: أصبح سنة لديهم وأصبح منكره منكرا للسنة
flags.context: فإذا تمسك به الناس وأخذ به عدد منهم أصبح سنة لديهم وأصبح منكره منكرا للسنة
options: it becomes a 'sunnah' in their eyes, and whoever rejects it becomes one who rejects the sunnah
it becomes an established practice among them, and its critic becomes a critic of the sunnah
it comes to count as sunnah with them, and to deny it is to deny the sunnah
flags.note: The sentence turns on the Sheikh using سنة in the loose sense of 'settled practice' while the people he describes take it in the technical sense. The scare quotes in the English carry that irony without asserting that the practice is sunnah. Flagged because dropping the quotes would make the corpus appear to call an innovation a sunnah.

options: the revealed laws and sound human nature
the revealed laws and innate dispositions (fiţar)
flags.note: Both nouns are plural in the Arabic. فطر is the plural of fiţrah, the innate constitution on which people are created; 'natural reason' would import a different concept. Flagged so a reviewer can fix a house rendering for fiţrah, which is not yet in the glossary.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

This page belongs to the Sheikh's tape series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, identified in article 516, the first tape of the series. Passages in quotation marks are the base text being commented on; the unquoted text is the Sheikh's own commentary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved.
The page carries no chapter heading; it opens mid-argument.
بنيات الطريق is the classical image of the minor tracks that branch off a main road. It is rendered by its sense rather than by a literal 'daughters of the road'.
The file for this tape on the site is L14.docx, and tape eight (article 511) links to L16.docx; the numbering of the attached documents does not run parallel to the tape numbers.
